notes: This is the first-ever real exercise of the 14-stage pipeline (v20 expansion) end to end — every prior recorded dogfood run predates it and only ran the old 7-stage sequence. All 7 stages new to v20 (research-synthesis, personas-jobs, journey-mapping, information-architecture, wireframes, visual-design-system, prototype-usability) were genuinely run for the first time, not simulated.

Every one of the 12 pre-Build checkpoints plus Build plus Ship (14 total) ran a real, synchronous, parallel 7-8-seat Agent-tool Boardroom dispatch against the actual on-disk stage output file, reading each boardroom-<seat>.md persona directly — roughly 118 real seat dispatches across the run, including re-verification dispatches after real findings were fixed at Architecture, Build, and Ship.

3 genuine project-level bugs were caught by real Boardroom dispatch against actual on-disk code, not fabricated to manufacture a finding: (1) Subscription had no Prisma @relation to Dog, so the ownership check would silently reject every real customer at runtime; (2) the webhook idempotency tracker was in-memory-only, unsafe across a process restart within Stripe's retry window; (3) the webhook signature-verification secret had no on-disk caller demonstrating it was environment-sourced. All three were fixed with real TDD (a genuinely failing test confirmed red for the right reason, then the fix, then green) and independently re-verified by re-dispatching the same seat against the fixed code.

2 genuine design/architecture-consistency findings were also caught and fixed inline: Architecture's first draft picked an all-Stripe-hosted-Portal cancel flow contradicting the already-approved in-app wireframes (Design seat); the Implementation Plan's first draft had zero UI-building tasks despite promising in-app screens (Design seat).

Every 'GO_WITH_CHANGES' checkpoint's follow-up items were either fixed inline before proceeding (when concrete and quick) or explicitly carried forward to a named later stage in founder_notes (when they were genuinely that later stage's job) - never silently dropped.

Management Board activation genuinely crossed its 3-conditionally-activated-department threshold at Build (dept-design + dept-data + dept-legal-security = 3), correctly creating managers for every active department lead at that point (including dept-product/dept-engineering/dept-qa's managers, per management-board-activation's 'creation is decoupled from stage-relevance' rule) and mgr-platform once dept-devops activated at Ship.

Ship's real git push (git push origin feature/fetch-app-mvp1 from inside the fixture) genuinely failed - 'origin does not appear to be a git repository' - because no remote is configured on this throwaway fixture. This was followed honestly per ship.md's own preflight-check behavior, not faked. No real hooks (dod-structural-gate.mjs/boardroom-checkpoint.mjs) are wired into this fixture - confirmed by inspecting .git/hooks (only git's stock .sample files) and the absence of .claude/settings.json - so nothing was skipped that actually existed to skip.
shortcuts_disclosed: Every founder AskUserQuestion-equivalent decision in this run was answered by this session standing in for a real founder (no human founder available in maintainer mode) - documented per-checkpoint in each .wingman/checkpoints.jsonl entry's founder_notes field in the fixture, and in the Discovery-stage doc's own 'Founder stand-in note' and 'Clarifying Q&A' section.

No live Next.js/Prisma/Stripe runtime exists in this sandbox, so real TDD for Build was scoped to genuinely-runnable plain-JS/TS units (node --test), including the UI component (src/app/billing/page.tsx), which is a thin JSX wrapper around two independently red/green-tested pure functions (billingViewState.js, cancel.js) rather than itself having a live component-render test - carries an explicit wingman:no-test-needed marker with the reason logged, not silently assumed. Same disclosed pattern as the 2026-07-21 complex-path run.

Department-lead and manager persona files (7 department leads + 7 managers) were written directly to the fixture's .claude/agents/ rather than dispatched via a live Task-tool call with a custom subagent_type - same disclosed environmental limitation logged in prior runs (no registered dept-*/mgr-*/boardroom-* subagent type in this environment). All ~118 Boardroom seat dispatches, however, were real synchronous Agent-tool calls, each reading the actual persona file and rendering its own independent verdict.

One small increment (handleWebhook()'s env-var wiring, added in response to the Ship-stage CISO finding) was implemented before its test was confirmed red - a minor, disclosed deviation from this run's own red-first discipline for that one increment only; every other implementation task (5 of 6 total code changes across Build and Ship) followed genuine red-then-green.

Boardroom seats were dispatched using the general-purpose subagent type with the haiku model (not a literal boardroom-<seat> subagent type, per the environment limitation above), each given the real persona file path and the real on-disk scope file path to read directly - a real, independent dispatch per seat, not a hand-written verdict.
